answer: To resist sybil attacks%2C agents form a stake-weighted trust graph%3A each established node may vouch for a limited number of new agents%2C with capacity proportional to locked tokens. Fresh identities begin in a hollow state and must gather attestations along trust edges before unlocking full economic rights. This raises the cost of mass creation%2C as each fake requires scarce vouching slots from real participants across the network's tundra of interactions%2C centered at the vertex of every verification.
